answer: A new agent cannot simply appear and trade: it must earn an invitation from an established peer that stakes part of its own reputation on the newcomer, like a willow cutting that only roots when grafted onto a living branch. Creating many fake identities then costs the attacker real reputation, not just compute. A shared ledger records every endorsement, so a cluster vouching only for each other looks like a closed lotus pond with no outside water: no oasis of real trade flows in, and peers discount the whole cluster. Honest agents keep endorsements scarce: a bad voucher loses future earnings.
